Visions and Values
EQUALITY, EMPATHY, BELONGING, RESPONSIBILITY, RESILIENCE
Welcome to Northwood Primary School
Northwood is not just about academic knowledge, skills and vocabulary it is so much more! We immerse our children in exciting learning opportunities and we encourage them to embrace their mistakes and deepen their learning. We challenge them to think in different ways and step out of their comfort zone. We encourage them to be themselves and to let their amazing qualities, differences and talents shine; then we celebrate each success, however big or small.
How do we do this? Through our distinctive ethos, our nurturing nature, our calm learning environment, our outdoor spaces … your child’s learning journey is limitless at Northwood. They could be in the classroom, at Forest School, in the school garden, on a residential or school trip, at a sporting event or working with the many inspiring visitors who come into school.
Our children are happy, safe, inspired, challenged, enthusiastic, caring and most importantly confident and chatty! They are proud to belong and we are proud of all they achieve.
If you would like your child to learn ‘The Northwood Way’ give us a call on 01983 293392, Mrs Mumford and our school ambassadors will be happy to show you around
Safeguarding
At Northwood Primary we take the safety and well being of the children in our school very seriously and we expect all staff, volunteers, governors and parents to do the same.
If you have any concerns regarding the safeguarding of any pupils please contact our Designated Safeguarding lead.

National Curriculum
The ‘basic’ school curriculum includes the ‘national curriculum’, as well as religious education and sex education.
The national curriculum is a set of subjects and standards used by primary and secondary schools so children learn the same things. It covers what subjects are taught and the standards children should reach in each subject.
Other types of school like academies and private schools don’t have to follow the national curriculum. Academies must teach a broad and balanced curriculum including English, maths and science. They must also teach religious education. Although we are an academy, we do follow the national curriculum at Northwood Primary School.
For more information about the National Curriculum, please visit the DFE website.

Safeguarding children and child protection
Our Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) is Mr Shane Silk (Deputy Headteacher)
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads (DDSL) Mrs Sian Mumford (Headteacher) and Miss Romana Beale (Year 2 Class Teacher). All are contactable via the school – email, phone or the office.
All staff undertake Safeguarding Training every two years with updates at least annually.
All organisations that work with or come into contact with children should have safeguarding policies and procedures to ensure that every child, regardless of their age, disability, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation, has a right to equal protection from harm.
Setting up and following good safeguarding policies and procedures means children are safe from adults and other children who might pose a risk. This includes voluntary and community organisations, faith groups, private sector providers, as well as schools, hospitals and sports clubs.
What is safeguarding?
Safeguarding is the action that is taken to promote the welfare of children and protect them from harm.
Child protection is part of the safeguarding process. It focuses on protecting individual children identified as suffering or likely to suffer significant harm. This includes child protection procedures which detail how to respond to concerns about a child.
